membership.reason: SSM_{PK-PD} is a treatment-conditioned latent state-space model using pharmacodynamic mechanistic inductive biases to model biomarker evolution under drug regimens.
membership.counting_boundary: Verified L2 action-conditioned pharmacodynamic world model (WT_PHYSIOLOGY; downgraded from L3 because evaluations cover observed-regimen conditional density and forward samples without matched alternative-regimen comparisons).

properties.backbone: Deep generative State Space Model (SSM_PK-PD) with PK-PD_Neural attention over mechanistic treatment-effect modules

properties.flow: Baseline covariates B + longitudinal biomarkers X_t + drug combinations U_t -> PK-PD_Neural latent state transition -> future biomarker distributions

properties.purpose: Treatment-conditioned chronic disease progression modeling and counterfactual/drug-effect analysis in multiple myeloma.
properties.environment: ML-MMRF CoMMpass multi-centre observational study + synthetic benchmarks

assertions.rationale: Explicitly handles frequent missingness in longitudinal laboratory biomarkers X_t.
Continuous latent disease-burden state evolving in state-space model.
Attention weights over competing mechanistic pharmacodynamic hypotheses provide interpretable insights.
Time-varying multi-drug treatment combinations U_t in R^L (binary or dosage).
Neural state-space model with pharmacodynamic mechanistic inductive biases.

Latent disease state transition is explicitly parameterized by time-varying drug combinations and local therapy clocks U_t and evaluated via held-out conditional density p(X|U,B) on synthetic and ML-MMRF cohorts (Table 1, p. 8), local-clock ablations (Figure 3), and treatment-conditioned forward biomarker trajectories (Figure 5, pp. 8-9).
Competing pharmacodynamic functional forms (PK-PD hypotheses) embedded as neural modules.

Evaluated sequential future biomarker prediction via held-out NELBO (61.54 vs 73.44-105.04 for baselines on 282 ML-MMRF test patients; pairwise win rates 0.714-0.934, Table 1) and forward multi-step biomarker trajectories conditioned on prior patient history and prescribed treatments (Figures 3 and 5, pp. 7-9).
Chronic disease progression modeling, drug-effect detection, and counterfactual exploration.
Held-out longitudinal biomarker density/trajectory generalization on ML-MMRF CoMMpass and synthetic data.
Generalization across treatment lines and cohorts in ML-MMRF.
Drug combination effects modeled in latent representation space.

evidence_fragments.content: Concretely, we aim to encourage neural models to learn representations that encode a patient’s underlying disease burden by specifying how these representations evolve due to treatment. We develop a new disease progression model that captures such insights by using inductive biases rooted in the biological mechanisms of treatment effect.

It learns to attend over multiple competing mechanistic explanations of how a patient’s genetics, past treatment history, and prior disease state influence the representation to predict the next outcome. The architecture is instantiated in a state space model, SSMPK-PD, and shows strong improvements in generalization compared to several baselines and prior state of the art.

First, we consistently observe that a high fraction of patient data in the test set are explained better by SSMPK-PD than the corresponding baseline (pairwise comparisons). We also note that out of 282 patients in the test set, across all the baselines, we find that the SSMPK-PD generalizes better for many more patients (counts).

SSMPK-PD better captures the evolution of these biomarkers conditioned on treatment. For serum IgG, SSMPK-PD correctly predicts the relapse of disease after stopping first line therapy, while SSMLinear does not. On the other hand, for serum lambda, SSMPK-PD correctly predicts it will remain steady.

capability_assessments.rationale: Downgraded honestly from L3 to L2 (consistent with legacy columns Z/AA): SSM_{PK-PD} implements persistent latent disease state (019), temporal state-space dynamics (041), and learned hybrid pharmacodynamic transitions (042), and evaluates action-conditioned longitudinal biomarker prediction (043, 053) on synthetic data and ML-MMRF (Table 1, Figures 3 & 5). No matched alternative-regimen counterfactual comparison (action.comparison) is reported in the 11-page PDF.

limitations: Observational ML-MMRF registry without prospective interventional validation.

Evaluates associational treatment-conditioned density and observed-regimen forward samples only; no matched alternative-regimen counterfactual comparison or causal identification is evaluated (supporting L2 rather than L3).
notes: All 11 physical PDF pages extracted/read; page 2 visually inspected via rendered PNG.

legacy_cells.C: Zeshan M Hussain, Rahul G. Krishnan, David Sontag
legacy_cells.S: How do a multiple-myeloma patient's latent disease state and clinical biomarkers evolve over time under specified treatment regimens?
legacy_cells.T: 1,143 patients with multiple myeloma from the MMRF CoMMpass study; patients were aligned to treatment start.
legacy_cells.AI: Structured clinical data: longitudinal biomarkers; baseline demographic and genomic covariates; treatment indicators and line-of-therapy inputs.
legacy_cells.AJ: Structured inference network with a bidirectional recurrent neural network.
legacy_cells.AN: Missing biomarker values are marginalized in the likelihood; forward-fill imputation is used for the inference network.
legacy_cells.AZ: The authors visualize latent states with t-SNE and report that later representations separate into groups associated with treatment status and coarse disease severity.
legacy_cells.BD: Five binary drug-prescription markers and a three-dimensional one-hot line-of-therapy encoding in the ML-MMRF data.
legacy_cells.BN: Attention selects among neural treatment-effect mechanisms inspired by pharmacology: bounded linear, neural log-cell-kill, and neural treatment-exponential functions; global and local therapy clocks encode elapsed time.
legacy_cells.BS: Predicted latent states are decoded into multivariate clinical biomarker observations using a Gaussian emission model.
legacy_cells.BV: Variational lower-bound / conditional-density training objective; the authors optimize negative log p(X|U,B) using ADAM.
legacy_cells.CG: Figure 5 reports averages of three forward samples from each model.
legacy_cells.DN: Synthetic disease-progression data; ML-MMRF (curated subset of the Multiple Myeloma Research Foundation CoMMpass study); semi-synthetic data (appendix).
legacy_cells.DQ: ML-MMRF: 1,143 patients; test set: 282 patients. Synthetic experiments trained on 100 or 1,000 samples and evaluated on five held-out sets of 50,000 each.
legacy_cells.EI: Compared with SSMLinear, SSMNL, SSMMOE, and SSMAttn.Hist. On ML-MMRF, the reported fractions of test patients with lower SSMPK-PD NELBO were 0.796, 0.760, 0.714, and 0.934, respectively; reported NELBO values were 61.54 for SSMPK-PD versus 74.22, 79.10, 73.44, and 105.04 for those baselines.
legacy_cells.EK: Ablations: setting the local clock constant (PK-PD without local clocks) and replacing the neural treatment-exponential mechanism (SSMPK-PD w/o TExp). The local-clock ablation did not capture treatment-response onset or persistence in the synthetic experiment.
legacy_cells.FB: Continuous latent patient-state vector inferred from longitudinal biomarkers, transitioned conditional on prior latent state, treatment, and baseline covariates.
legacy_cells.FL: A bidirectional recurrent inference network estimates continuous stochastic latent patient states from biomarker histories; an action- and baseline-conditioned transition attends over three pharmacology-inspired neural mechanisms, and a Gaussian emission decoder generates biomarkers. No planner is evaluated.
legacy_cells.FM: Introduces PK-PDNeural, an attention-based family of pharmacology-inspired treatment-effect mechanisms, and instantiates it as the SSMPK-PD state-space model; evaluates its generalization on synthetic and ML-MMRF data and releases the ML-MMRF benchmark and code.
legacy_cells.FN: On ML-MMRF, SSMPK-PD test NELBO was 61.54 versus 105.04 for SSMAttn.Hist.; SSMPK-PD had lower NELBO for 0.934 of test patients in that pairwise comparison, and the >10-nat counts were 272 versus 0 (out of 282). The authors also report significant generalization gains over baselines on synthetic data, especially with 100 training samples.
legacy_cells.FO: The authors caution that using multiple copies of mechanism functions must be balanced against potential overfitting on small datasets.
legacy_cells.FP: The authors propose applying the model to other chronic diseases with disease-specific neural PK-PD functions and using it to build parametric environment simulators.
legacy_cells.FQ: The authors identify that black-box sequential models commonly concatenate treatments to hidden representations, leaving the network to learn treatment effects; such approaches can struggle to capture treatment responses when clinical data are scarce.
legacy_cells.FR: The model demonstrates treatment-conditioned prediction of observed biomarker trajectories and internal held-out predictive performance. It does not establish causal identification for alternative regimens, test a treatment planner or decision policy, or report prospective or external clinical validation; conditioning on observational prescriptions is not evidence of causal counterfactual effects.
